executive_assessment.text: District/gewog indices identify differentiated vulnerability, while Dechencholing and Punakha cases show historical displacement and service-access losses; indices are older and cases are not representative.
Water-system delivery gaps and women's participation barriers add institutional depth. Mobility evidence is anecdotal and wildlife interactions are not human FCV.

geographic_notes.text: The2022 vulnerability assessment's present-risk index ranks Samtse, Monggar, Sarpang, Punakha and Dagana highest using older administrative indicators; not a2026risk or loss ranking.
The2022 assessment gives Zhemgang, Dagana and Gasa the lowest adaptive-capacity index scores; slower recovery is an inference, not measured outcomes.
The2022 assessment ranks Lunana gewog in Gasa highest in socioeconomic vulnerability, citing low electricity and roughly19%concrete housing in its underlying data.
Thimphu is projected as the highest future-risk area, associated with in-migration, urbanisation and population growth.
The2025 loss-and-damage report describes the2024 Dechencholing flood displacing84families, temporarily closing two schools and killing one person, with wellbeing and cohesion consequences.
2025 Punakha floods cut Gasa road access for over two weeks; bridge loss affected 42 households, while budget gaps delayed response and residents supplied most repair labour.
The2026 ACREWAS midterm review reports11,544beneficiaries (45.7%female),3,220trained people and4,426hectares under climate-resilient management; these are interim programme indicators.
At the2026 ACREWAS midterm, assured irrigation/domestic-water access reached5.6%of its interim target, with systems still under construction; final water-service benefits were not yet measurable.

The2026 ACREWAS review describes women interested in water-user associations but constrained by gender roles, lower formal education and care burdens; sustained participation effects were not evaluated.

known_gaps.text: The inspected sources do not establish a country-specific climate-conflict or climate-violence pathway.
The World Bank page is an official summary; the underlying CCDR modeling details and named scenario pathways were not inspected.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
No inspected source establishes climate-driven interpersonal, communal or political violence in Bhutan. The assessment's human-wildlife-conflict finding is not evidence of human social violence.
The climate-to-distress-mobility statement is described by the assessment as anecdotal; it gives no movement counts and does not link migration to later conflict.

The district vulnerability assessment uses older indicators, reports sparse annual Dzongkhag/Gewog data and uncertain cause-and-effect relationships; its rankings are not a current complete local survey.
The loss-and-damage assessment says loss records are fragmented and underreported; the Dechencholing and Punakha findings are case studies, not representative estimates.

The ACREWAS review is limited to three project Dzongkhags and a midterm period. Assured water access was not yet measurable as a household outcome, and the Gasa labor-influx passage identifies potential safeguards risks rather than reported incidents.
The World Bank CCDR and 2024 NCHM climate-projection PDF exceeded the browser tool's content limit; neither was used to support a claim.
Generic Gasa labor-influx safeguard risks were excluded as local climate-FCV evidence; no actual incidents or climate-mediated chain was established.
Human-wildlife conflict is livelihood sensitivity, not human social violence.
The coordinator could not reopen the evaluation endpoint; its bounded findings rely on the collector's full-text extraction and should receive human source recheck before approval.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
